verses.1: The Queen of Sheba had heard of the name of Solomon for the reputation of the LORD, and she came to test him with riddles.
verses.2: She came to Jerusalem with a great retinue, many camels bearing spices and a very large amount of gold and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.
verses.3: Solomon answered her with all her questions; there was no question that he did not answer for her.
verses.4: And the Queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house that he had built.
verses.5: The food at his table, the seating of his servants, the standing of his attendants in their uniforms, his cupbearers and their goblets, and the burnt offerings he brought at the house of the LORD—there was no breath left in her.
verses.6: She said to the king: "The truth of what I heard in my country about your words and your wisdom was real,
verses.7: but I did not believe those reports until I came. And now, your half was not what I heard—what you have added to it in goodness is even greater than the report I heard."
verses.8: Happy are your servants, happy are your attendants who stand before you continually, hearing your wisdom!
verses.9: May the LORD your God be praised, who delighted in you to place you on the throne of Israel, for the LORD loves Israel forever. He has made you king to do justice and righteousness."
verses.10: And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great abundance and precious stones. Never again came such an amount of spices as what the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.11: The ship of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought cedar and juniper trees in very great abundance and precious stones.
verses.12: The king made the cedar into supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. Such cedar trees had not been seen or come into the land before that day.
verses.13: And King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba all that she desired, beyond what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her attendants.
verses.14: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.15: in addition to the tribute of the merchants and all the kings of the regions and the officials of the land.
verses.16: Solomon made two hundred shields of beaten gold, each shield weighing six hundred shekels of gold.
verses.17: And three hundred shields of hammered gold, each shield weighing three minas of gold. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
verses.18: The king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
verses.19: The throne had six steps, with a lion carved on either side at the back of the throne, and two lions standing by the arms.
verses.20: Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on either side. No throne like this was made for any other kingdom.
verses.21: All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were gold, and all the vessels in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were gold. Nothing was made of silver in Solomon's days—it had no value.
verses.22: For a ship from Tarshish came to the king by sea with the ships of Hiram. Once every three years the ship from Tarshish brought gold and silver, ivory, and apes and peacocks.
verses.23: And King Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
verses.24: All the earth sought the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had placed in his heart.
verses.25: And they brought each year their tribute—silver vessels, gold vessels, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules—according to the year, year by year.
verses.26: Solomon gathered together chariots and horses; he had a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he kept in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.27: And the king set the silver in Jerusalem as if it were stones, and the cedars he set as if they were common timbers in abundance.
verses.28: The horses that Solomon had came from Egypt and from Kue, the merchants of the king taking them at a price.
verses.29: A chariot came up from Egypt for six hundred silver shekels, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. And so it was for all the kings of the Hittites and for the kings of Aram in their hands.

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "there was no breath left in her" translates the Hebrew idiom meaning she was overwhelmed or awestruck.
- v. 11: "cedar and juniper trees" — the Hebrew uses "almugim," a term of uncertain botanical identity; "juniper" is a plausible rendering.
- v. 12: "harps and lyres for the singers" — the Hebrew uses the words "kinor" and "nevel," which are standard terms for stringed instruments.
- v. 16-17: The weights are translated literally without attempting to convert to metric or imperial equivalents.
- v. 27: "as if they were stones" and "as if they were common timbers" — the Hebrew uses a simile to emphasize the abundance and low value of these materials.
- v. 28: "Kue" is a variant spelling of "Kush" or "Ethiopia" in some manuscripts.

[1] The Queen of Sheba had heard of the name of Solomon for the reputation of the LORD, and she came to test him with riddles.  
[2] She came to Jerusalem with a great retinue, many camels bearing spices and a very large amount of gold and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.  
[3] Solomon answered her with all her questions; there was no question that he did not answer for her.  
[4] And the Queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house that he had built.  
[5] The food at his table, the seating of his servants, the standing of his attendants in their uniforms, his cupbearers and their goblets, and the burnt offerings he brought at the house of the LORD—there was no breath left in her.  
[6] She said to the king: "The truth of what I heard in my country about your words and your wisdom was real,  
[7] but I did not believe those reports until I came. And now, your half was not what I heard—what you have added to it in goodness is even greater than the report I heard."  
[8] Happy are your servants, happy are your attendants who stand before you continually, hearing your wisdom!  
[9] May the LORD your God be praised, who delighted in you to place you on the throne of Israel, for the LORD loves Israel forever. He has made you king to do justice and righteousness."  
[10] And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great abundance and precious stones. Never again came such an amount of spices as what the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.  
[11] The ship of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought cedar and juniper trees in very great abundance and precious stones.  
[12] The king made the cedar into supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and into harps and lyres for the singers. Such cedar trees had not been seen or come into the land before that day.  
[13] And King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba all that she desired, beyond what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her attendants.  
[14] Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,  
[15] in addition to the tribute of the merchants and all the kings of the regions and the officials of the land.  
[16] Solomon made two hundred shields of beaten gold, each shield weighing six hundred shekels of gold.  
[17] And three hundred shields of hammered gold, each shield weighing three minas of gold. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.  
[18] The king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.  
[19] The throne had six steps, with a lion carved on either side at the back of the throne, and two lions standing by the arms.  
[20] Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on either side. No throne like this was made for any other kingdom.  
[21] All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were gold, and all the vessels in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were gold. Nothing was made of silver in Solomon's days—it had no value.  
[22] For a ship from Tarshish came to the king by sea with the ships of Hiram. Once every three years the ship from Tarshish brought gold and silver, ivory, and apes and peacocks.  
[23] And King Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.  
[24] All the earth sought the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had placed in his heart.  
[25] And they brought each year their tribute—silver vessels, gold vessels, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules—according to the year, year by year.  
[26] Solomon gathered together chariots and horses; he had a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he kept in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.  
[27] And the king set the silver in Jerusalem as if it were stones, and the cedars he set as if they were common timbers in abundance.  
[28] The horses that Solomon had came from Egypt and from Kue, the merchants of the king taking them at a price.  
[29] A chariot came up from Egypt for six hundred silver shekels, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. And so it was for all the kings of the Hittites and for the kings of Aram in their hands.
